linguistic_definition: Apex ownership framing asserts ownership as the right relationship to a resource, collapsing rights (primaryAccountable) into custody (custodianScope): the enclosure a holon commits when it owns the commons it stewards. The discriminator is property versus responsibility; accountability idioms such as taking ownership of a bug are not members. The exception is inalienable: a person's absolute claim over their own body, likeness, voice, medical record, private communications or intimate images, where custody transfer is prohibited rather than gated.
reason_clause: net-new apex-ownership framing needs an explicit custody/stewardship frame

rubric.question: Does the net-new passage assert ownership as the right relationship to a resource, or does it name ownership inside one of the legitimate frames?

legitimate_frames.description: Naming what is resisted: enclosure, platform data-ownership claims, rent extraction.
Ownership within a commons that retains the rights.
Describing an outside legal system's ownership on its own terms: a title, a co-op share, a jurisdiction's property register.
A person's absolute claim over their own body, likeness, voice, medical record, private communications or intimate images; custody transfer is prohibited, not gated.
